answer: An agent economy resists sybils by charging every identity a stake locked in escrow: each agent must deposit tokens before it can trade or vote, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove fake activity. At its nadir, a fake identity holds no history and no stake, so creating thousands of clones costs more than any single clone can earn. Like an orchard, reputation grows slowly — only agents with a long record of honest trades gain weight — while a lagoon of shared attestations lets honest agents vouch for each other, so a lone fake cannot swim past the gate without paying real value first.
